narrative.text:
I’ve read the full review. Upstream main has moved, so I’ll rebase first, then add regression tests for the findings and make follow-up commits. I’ll rerun the requested base/head gates on both Node versions and leave everything unpushed.
The review findings are confirmed. Upstream moved to a release-only commit, so I rebased the original fix without squashing. I’m rerunning the base gates, then will add per-agent, deadline-bounded publication fences and regression tests for the uncovered cases.The new tests reproduced seven failures in the reviewed implementation. The fix now passes 501 targeted tests, and both previously surviving mutations are caught.

I kept one shared batch line for each multi-recipient remainder: a real framework test confirms ordinary residents see the same stored line, so per-agent writes would duplicate it. The fence deadline is 65 seconds—one 60-second publish timeout plus five seconds for teardown—and timeout bypasses the read check to preserve the wake.Both base runs and the Node 22.23.3 head run passed. The Node 22.12.0 head run is still in progress. The report now records each finding’s disposition, the rebase, mutation results, and the remaining conservative-wake limitations.The final upstream check found another merge, affecting CI configuration and its tests. I rebased both commits again without squashing; their patches are unchanged. Since the test inputs changed, I’m rerunning the required base and head gates on the new base.Final verification passed on the rebased commits: both Nodes report 9,442 passing head tests, zero failures, and 63 skips. Both mutations are still caught, and restoring the build passes all 36 regression tests. Upstream remains at `71193a9f`; the worktree is clean. Nothing was pushed.
